packages.headline: Fear The Timeloop Brings a Deadly 15 Minute Loop to XBOX

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
A discussion of the function of time and the meaning of repetitive death in Fear The Timeloop.
Fear The Timeloop Brings a Deadly 15 Minute Loop to XBOX
When I began working on Fear The Timeloop , I wanted to make time feel physically important. It could not be a timer that simply sits in the corner of the screen. Every minute needed to be something you could lose, earn, or spend too early.
On September 4, Fear The Timeloop comes to Xbox Series X|S. You play as Sheriff James Cooper, who wakes up in Saint Heritage Hospital with a severe abdominal wound. He is slowly bleeding out. If James cannot find a way to keep himself alive within 15 minutes, he dies, and the loop begins again.
In Fear The Timeloop , the countdown is inseparable from survival. James’ health and remaining time are one resource. Every minute takes him closer to death from blood loss.
Blood bags, first aid kits, bandages, and other medical supplies do more than repair the damage from an enemy attack. They buy James more time. A familiar survival horror item can change an entire attempt. Do you use it now to cross a dangerous corridor safely? Save it in case a fight becomes unavoidable? Or risk those precious minutes to explore a room that may reveal a new path?
The 15-minute loop grew out of that idea. I did not want a timer only to create pressure. I wanted it to shape every decision while staying grounded in the game’s world. James does not die because of an arbitrary rule. He dies because he is bleeding out.
I also wanted death to be more than a punishment. When James dies, he returns to the beginning of the current chapter, marked by a VHS tape he has found. But he does not return to absolute zero.
After every attempt, the notes you have discovered, your map data, and unlocked abilities remain. Your inventory does not. You can remember a code, discover a hidden route, or unlock a new ability, but you must still rethink your resources and survival plan in the next loop.

packages.headline: 'It Definitely Was a Shock': The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Artwork Splits Fans Following Trailer Reveal

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
What do you think of the new art style for Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake? It's the big question that fans have been discussing ever since today's Zelda Direct — and now they're poring over new artwork, too.
'It Definitely Was a Shock': The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Artwork Splits Fans Following Trailer Reveal
Looking over social media commentary alongside the Direct itself, there was a fair amount of surprise at how different this version of Nintendo's N64 classic actually looked. Of course, the visuals in this ground-up Ocarina remake have been given a vast upgrade. But the visual style employed here by Nintendo looks unlike any other Zelda game seen to date.
The intent here, I think, is to create something that bridges the gap between the Switch 2's technical capability while retaining the slightly exaggerated and angular aesthetic of the N64 original. There's also a conscious decision not to turn this version of Ocarina into something it's not — a cel-shaded game, something stylized in the same fashion as Breath of the Wild, or even the grittier 3D tones of Twilight Princess.
Of course, not everyone is a fan. "They Cocomelon'd all of them 😞," wrote one fan, examining the character artwork that Nintendo has now released via Ocarina of Time's Japanese website (check it out in the slideshow of images above). "Kid Link looks like a goldfish," wrote another.
"It's not a bad design, but I grew up with the original, so the new designs just look too busy," wrote a third, who seemed to sit more on the fence. "I think that if I wasn't so familiar with the original I might like them a bit more."
Particular criticism seems to be being levelled at Young Link and Young Zelda, who have kept some of the stylized dimensions of their N64 designs (big foreheads!) while also now appearing far more detailed.
"I hate how wet and greebled Child Link looks, the voice acting and cutscenes seem abysmal, and Kokiri Forest looks gross, but otherwise it seems kind of great," wrote one fan with strong opinions. "The sizzle reel at the end looked unbelievably good. They should've started with that."

Call of Duty Adds Doom Slayer Skin as Part of New Halloween Update
Call of Duty's upcoming Halloween event will add the Doom Slayer to the game as a playable operator.
As part of what is expected to be the final season of content for Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, Activision is adding in one of the most iconic protagonists in FPS history: the Doom Slayer. The character will be added as part of The Haunting update, which will be released on September 17. Players will be able to acquire the Doom Slayer operator, inspired by Doom: The Dark Ages, as well as a Doomguy skin which is more in line with the character's look from the original Doom games. Of course, this will all be rounded out with signature Doom weaponry, including the shotgun, crucible blade, and the almighty BFG.
The legendary FPS icon will be added on September 24 via an event pass, which players can purchase. There will also be a free tier which will include various items, such as Doom-inspired skins like a UAC scientist and reseracher, weapon charms, and more. The premium tier will have the Doom Slayer operator skin and the more sought after weapon blueprints.
The Haunting update will include a variety of other non-Doom content, including a nighttime version of the Avalon map, spooky content and foes in Black Ops 7's Endgame mode, limited-time multiplayer modes, and new maps. It's one last hoorah for Black Ops 7 ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release in October, so be sure to hop in and check it out while it lasts.
Black Ops 7 is one of the lesser-recieved Call of Duty games , having launched with a poor campaign and a multiplayer mode that yielded mixed results from the community. The title was partially overshadowed by strong competition such as Battlefield 6 and Arc Radiers, but Treyarch has done its best to support the game with a steady stream of content and updated the game to implement player feedback. The open comms have also rubbed off on Infinity Ward, which has led to Modern Warfare 4 being fine tuned with the community in mind .

sources.label: IGN Games

The Trump Administration appears to have pulled its Tetris clone 'Build the Wall' offline less than one week after its launch.
Trump Administration Tetris Clone Vanishes from White House Website Days After Launch
The Trump Administration appears to have pulled its 'Build the Wall' Tetris clone offline less than one week after its launch .
The title launched last week alongside a small collection of other games as part of yet another attempt from The White House to connect with U.S. gamers. Build the Wall has now vanished from the Arcade.Gov website (as spotted by VGC ), while the four other games it launched alongside it remain.
Those who did try Build the Wall suggested it was clearly aimed to offend, not entertain. Aside from the criticism it received for its subject matter, which asked players to "protect the border from the incoming horde," players quickly realized the game itself didn't seem to be winnable at all. Instead of clearing filled lines, blocks would only continue to fall into place until reaching an inevitable ‘game over’ message when the screen was filled.
We don't know why the Tetris clone has disappeared, but we do know what followed after the Trump Administration launched Arcade.Gov. The website, which was marketed on social media with references to other gaming companies like Nintendo and Sega, quickly resulted in backlash online. The noise grew so loud so quickly that it didn't take long for The Tetris Company to respond.
"At Tetris, we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it said. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."
P.S. The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of ‘Build the Wall’. P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously. pic.twitter.com/Fu02khRpT3
Although The Tetris Company also said it takes "copyright infringement very seriously," it did not detail any specific plans to take action against Build the Wall. It elaborated on its feelings in a statement sent to The Verge at the time.

Justdan International has announced Tianji: Shadow of the Ancients , an internally developed turn-based RPG directed by “the father of the Xuan-Yuan Sword series.” It will launch for PlayStation 5 , Switch 2 , Switch , and PC via Steam in 2027 with English, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language options.

This delivers both the satisfying impact of an action game and deep strategic play. Players will step into the shoes of the amnesiac protagonist, Shangguan Shuo. packages.headline: “ハエの脳の配線図“が公開され、すぐさま『DOOM』のプレイに使われる。「被ダメージ」を学習して生き残りを目指す

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
HHMI Janelia ResearchおよびGoogle Researchは9月3日、オスのショウジョウバエの脳および中枢神経系全体のマッピングを公開。それを活用し、『DOOM』のゲームプレイのシミュレーションを行う人物がさっそく登場したようだ。
“ハエの脳の配線図“が公開され、すぐさま『DOOM』のプレイに使われる。「被ダメージ」を学習して生き残りを目指す
HHMI（ハワード・ヒューズ医学研究所） Janelia ResearchおよびGoogle Researchは9月3日、オスのショウジョウバエの脳および中枢神経系全体のマッピングを公開、発表した。同プロジェクトに関してはデータセットとしてMaleCNS v1.0がすでに公開されており、このデータを用いてさっそく「ハエに『DOOM』をプレイさせたらどうなるか」のシミュレーションをおこなうプロジェクトも発足しているようだ。
そんなオスのショウジョウバエのコネクトーム「MaleCNS v1.0」だが、これを用いて『DOOM』をプレイさせようとする試み「DOOMFLY」が実行されているようだ。『DOOM』は、id SoftwareがMS-DOS向けに開発し、1993年に発売されたFPSである。FPSというジャンルを世に知らしめた代表的な存在だ。
「DOOMFLY」と名付けられたこのシミュレーションを実施しているのは、CoinbaseのエンジニアであるAlex Wormuth氏だ。シミュレーションではまず『DOOM』の画面情報を、ハエが受け取れるような信号へと変換。そして入力された信号は、MaleCNS v1.0を元に構築された神経回路モデル内でニューロンの活動を呼び起こす。発生した活動は既定のコントローラー操作に対応している。
たとえばDNp20というニューロンの活動が旋回運動に、DNpe017の活動が前進および射撃に割り当てられているといったかたちだ。つまり疑似的に、ハエの脳や神経系が『DOOM』のゲーム画面を見てコントローラーを操作する、という状況を作りあげているわけだ。そして“ハエ”が操作しているプレイヤーがダメージを受けるとマイナスの報酬として、ドーパミン細胞に人工的な嫌悪刺激が送られるとのこと。そしてゲーム内で死を迎えると、新たに再挑戦がおこなわれる。これを繰り返し、ハエの脳や神経系を模したモデルで『DOOM』を“学習”できるのかを実証しようとしているわけだ。
I'm training a fly brain to play Doom using the full MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome. Each Doom frame stimulates sensory neurons. Neural activity is mapped to game controls. Damage triggers a stimulus to two PPL101 dopamine cells as reinforcement. Will the fly learn to… https://t.co/ObCJ03gxy3 pic.twitter.com/H2YDBtyuR8
『DOOM』については、現在ゲームエンジンのソースコードの利用・改変・再配布などを条件付きで認める「GPL-2.0」ライセンスで一般公開されている。そのためさまざまな媒体への移植が試みられていることでも有名だ。また『DOOM』をAIにプレイさせる試みのほか、『Doom II: Hell on Earth』を実験用ラットに“プレイ”させる試みも話題となった（ 関連記事 ）。今回は実際のハエを用いた実験とは異なるものの、デジタル化された生物の神経回路をゲームに投入するといった点で興味深い。
ショウジョウバエは俗に“コバエ”としても呼ばれるハエの一種だ。赤い目をもち、体長は2～3ミリメートル程度。生後10日程度で卵から成虫になるという特徴や、染色体が4対で生物の中でも目立って少ない。さらに餌の費用も安く済む傾向などから、特にDrosophila melanogaster（キイロショウジョウバエ）が実験生物として生物学の研究に盛んに用いられている。
HHMI Janelia ResearchおよびGoogle Researchは、このショウジョウバエのオスについて、脳と中枢神経系の“配線図”にあたるコネクトームを公開。メスについてはFlyWireコンソーシアムがコネクトームをすでに公開、発表しているため、今回のHHMI Janelia ResearchおよびGoogle Researchの取り組みによって、雌雄のショウジョウバエのコネクトームが揃ったことになる。なおこのデータセットは、オープンソースツールNeuroglancerを通じ、誰でも閲覧やダウンロードが可能になっている。

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
Draknek and Friendsは9月3日、Bobby Vanden氏が手がける『He Who Watches』を配信開始した。
“重力操作”弓パズル『He Who Watches』、Steamで「非常に好評」の好発進。壁も天井も歩き放題、『FEZ』などの影響受ける新たなひらめきゲーム
パブリッシャーのDraknek and Friendsは9月3日、Bobby Vanden氏が手がける『 He Who Watches 』を配信開始した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam/itch.io）で、ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。本作は重力操作を軸とする一風変わったパズル設計が支持され、Steamユーザーレビューでは「非常に好評」ステータスを獲得している。
『He Who Watches』は、空間認知と視点の切り替えを題材とする一人称視点のパズルゲームだ。舞台となるのは、数々のパズルと秘密が隠された古代の迷宮。迷宮の中心には“神”が囚われており、床だけでなく壁や天井まで足場として利用しながら、奥へと進んでいく。
『He Who Watches』は配信後から着実に評価を集め、本稿執筆時点でSteamユーザーレビュー64件中95％が好評とする「非常に好評」ステータスを獲得している。本作は、重力の向きとブロックの位置関係を読み解き、限られた仕組みを組み合わせながら解法を探していくパズル設計が持ち味だ。オブジェクト同士がどう作用するのかを見抜き、解法の核となるアイデアに気づけば一気に突破口が開ける、ひらめき重視のパズルゲームとなっている。また、メインのパズルとは別に用意された秘密や、迷宮に仕込まれた謎解きを楽しんでいるプレイヤーもいるようだ。
『He Who Watches』の開発を手がけるBobby Vanden氏は、アメリカを拠点とする個人デベロッパーだ。本作ではゲームデザイン、プログラム、アートを担当し、音楽は作曲家のAndré Frauenstein氏が手がけている。Vanden氏は、開発の舞台裏を紹介する 動画 も公開しており、プレイテストでは各パズルについて、挑戦した人数やクリアした人数、成功率、平均/中央値の所要時間、ヒントの使用数などを記録。大量のパズルを表計算上で一覧化することで、序盤の導線や難度を調整してきたという。また、本作は約4年にわたって制作されてきた作品だという。
100種類以上のパズルだけでなく、その周囲にも秘密を散りばめた『He Who Watches』。床・壁・天井という区別までひっくり返す独特の重力パズルが、今後どのように評価を広げていくか注目したい。
『He Who Watches』はPC（ Steam / itch.io ）向けに配信中。Steamではリリース記念セールとして、9月17日までは定価から15％オフとなる税込2125円で購入できる。ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。
本作で頼りとなるのは、弓と一本の魔法の矢だ。ただし、弓は敵を倒すための武器ではなく、周囲の環境を操るための道具となる。矢を使ってブロックを動かしたり、スイッチを作動させたりできるほか、矢と自身をつなぐ魔法の鎖を利用し、離れた足場へ移動することも可能だ。

『Path of Exile』を手がけてきたChris Wilson氏は、自身のYouTubeチャンネルにて「データマイニング」に対する見解と対策を紹介している。
『Path of Exile』にはデータマイナーをだます“偽データ”まで仕込んでいた、でも当時のボスいわく「かなり時間の無駄だった」。解析されまくる時代で、秘密を守る苦労
ハクスラARPG『Path of Exile』を手がけてきたChris Wilson氏は、自身のYouTubeチャンネルにて「データマイニング」に対する見解と対策を紹介している。そのなかには、“おとり”アセットをデータ内に組み込むなど、ユニークな対応もあったようだ。しかしこの対策には問題もあったとし、一筋縄ではいかないデータマイニングへの対応について伝えている。

CD PROJEKT REDは9月9日、販売中の『ウィッチャー３ ワイルドハント コンプリートエディション』について、PC/XBOX/Nintendo Switchでの販売価格を調整した。PC/XBOXではわずかながら値下げとなっている。
『ウィッチャー３ ワイルドハント コンプリートエディション』、価格改定でPC＆XBOX版が“ちょっとだけ値下がり”。リマスター版が出るので
CD PROJEKT REDは9月9日、販売中の『ウィッチャー３ ワイルドハント コンプリートエディション』について、各プラットフォームでの販売価格を調整した。本稿執筆時点ですでに価格は調整されており、XBOXおよびPC向けには値下げ、Nintendo Switch向けには値上げとなっている。
『ウィッチャー3』は、怪物退治を生業とするウィッチャー、リヴィアのゲラルトを主人公としたオープンワールドRPGだ。スラヴ神話をもとにした架空のファンタジー世界を舞台に、各地で依頼を受けながら探索と戦闘を重ねていく。クエストの達成によって能力や装備を強化でき、物語は選択によって展開や結末が変化する。

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
コーエーテクモゲームスは9月8日、『カリアのアトリエ ～夜の王国と追憶の道標～』を2月25日に発売すると告知した。
『カリアのアトリエ』来年2月25日発売へ。「なんでも食べる主人公」のオープンフィールド探索
コーエーテクモゲームスは9月8日、『 カリアのアトリエ ～夜の王国と追憶の道標～（以下、カリアのアトリエ） 』を2月25日に発売すると告知した。対応プラットフォームはPS5/Xbox Series X|S/Nintendo Switch 2/PC（Steam）で、通常版の価格は税込9680円。あわせて、新しい情報やPVなども公開されている。
『カリアのアトリエ』は、なんでも食べる主人公が錬金術とアクションを駆使して世界を冒険する、オープンフィールドを採用した錬金術RPGである。本作は、コーエーテクモゲームスのガストブランドによる「アトリエ」シリーズの最新作であり、「追憶」シリーズの2作目となる。前作にあたる『ユミアのアトリエ ～追憶の錬金術士と幻創の地～』では、錬金術が禁忌とされる世界を舞台に、錬金術士ユミア・リースフェルトがアラディス大陸へ出発。かつて錬金術によって栄えて滅んだという大国にまつわる失われた歴史を追う旅が、フィールドの探索やアイテムの調合などとともに描かれていた。銃を使った採取や2段ジャンプを含むアクション、ランダムクエストなど、オープンフィールド型の遊びを搭載していた点も大きな特徴だろう。
本作『カリアのアトリエ』では、錬金術士ユミアがアラディス大陸の謎を解き明かしてから2年後、アラディスで大陸のマナが減少する「マナ枯れ」が発生していた。主人公のカリアは「万物を食べてその特徴を知る」能力をもつ、記憶喪失の冒険者。生活のためアラディス開拓団に加わった彼女は、遺構の調査中に広大な地下世界を発見し、巨大な釜を用いた錬金術と出会う。伝承と過去に向き合う、追憶の物語が繰り広げられるという。
『 カリアのアトリエ 』はPS5/Xbox Series X|S/Nintendo Switch 2/PC（Steam）向けに、2月25日発売予定だ。通常版の価格は税込9680円で、早期購入特典として「カリアスペシャルコスチューム」や専用装備「訓練用メタルバッジ」が付属する。

packages.headline: 40 Changes We Noticed in the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gameplay Footage

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Here are 40 changes we saw when comparing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 to the N64 version, from things as large as the art style all the way to small menu changes and UI differences.
40 Changes We Noticed in the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gameplay Footage
Nintendo showed roughly 20 minutes of footage from the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time in the Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct this morning . Producer Eiji Aonuma said this project is largely a faithful remake of the N64 classic, reborn on Switch 2 with modern controls and a strong focus on detail. But even though the remake appears to stick closely to the bones of its source material, there are plenty of minor additions and changes I noticed when scrubbing back through the footage for a couple of hours following the Direct.
Here are 40 changes I saw when comparing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 to the N64 version, from things as large as the art style all the way to small menu changes and UI differences. This list mostly goes in chronological order, starting with the gameplay demonstration from Aonuma and ending with the new trailer that closed the presentation.
A brief warning : I talk in general terms about some items and locations from the original Ocarina of Time. So, if you want absolutely zero knowledge of these things before playing for yourself, stay away!
Obviously, the biggest difference in the remake is its visuals. Aonuma opened his gameplay demo with a look at Kokiri Forest, where the game begins. Everything is more detailed: there are paved stone paths, defined wooden staircases that used to be low-texture ramps, grass blowing in the wind, forest spirits gliding through the air, and modern sunlight seeping through the trees. It's definitely a brand new take on the first 3D Hyrule, especially compared to the 3DS version that essentially just spruced up the original visuals.
Link himself has seen a similarly significant overhaul. We saw lots of Child Link in the gameplay — with snippets of Adult Link showing up in the full trailer later on — and he looks a lot different. His woven green tunic has multiple layers now, with patterns sewn in and flourishes at the bottom. He wears a feather in his hair and has various beads throughout his outfit. I personally love how Link looks now. I think the uncanny art style of the blocky N64 originally shines through brilliantly in this interpretation. We see his mannerisms throughout the gameplay — like stretching when he's left idle for too long, or putting his hands on his hips when speaking to someone — and I think he perfectly embodies the spirit of the Hero of Time.
N64 Ocarina sets you off with a pretty small wallet that can only hold 99 rupees. That's pretty annoying, especially when you open a treasure chest that contains a high-value rupee that you aren't able to fit in your wallet, making it go to waste. On Switch 2, we see Link dive down and grab a blue rupee (worth five, of course) and add it to his wallet, which is shown to have a maximum capacity of 200. I'm sure we'll still upgrade our wallets through the Gold Skulltula questline, but this is a much better start!
On the left side of the new equipment screen, we see a grid of four empty slots (Link just doesn't have the matching items at the start of the game) that appear to be mapped to the top and bottom directional buttons on the left Joy-Con (or the D-pad on the Pro Controller). Later in the gameplay, we see that the Ocarina and Navi are each mapped to one of the left and right directional buttons, but the top and bottom are blank. It would appear that these are going to be shortcuts for equipment earned later in the adventure. I have to imagine this is the solution for swapping boots on the fly (more on that later), but I'm puzzled at what the other slots could be for, given that there are only two special sets of boots to find in the original. We'll have to wait and see.

packages.headline: AMC Theaters Is Broadcasting the 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals at Select Cinemas Across the US

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
The 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals will be broadcast at 50 AMC Theaters across the United States.
AMC Theaters Is Broadcasting the 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals at Select Cinemas Across the US
The Finals take place on Sunday, September 20. That day, fans can show up to participating AMC Theaters nationwide and catch the action on the big screen.
The competition will stream live from Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, Texas, where 20 teams will throw down for the chance to win $300,000 out of a staggering $1.2 million prize pool. The total broadcast will last approximately eight hours.
Tickets are currently on sale at participating theaters, with adult tickets priced at $19.49 ($22.18 if booked online). Only a few of these theaters are showing the Finals, and tickets are selling out fast, so make sure to grab yours quickly if you want a front row seat to see who gets crowned the 15th Rocket League World Champions.
Most major esports tournaments are streamed on Twitch, with viewers receiving special drops that can be earned by simply watching on the platform. AMC Theaters has already thought of this, and is giving fans commemorative Rocket League tickets that include codes to redeem the drops that they would normally get watching the competition on Twitch.
“Such a big part of the magic of movie theatres is their ability to bring people together for unforgettable shared experiences, and a live event like the Rocket League World Championship is a great example of that," Ellen Copaken, SVP of Business Development for AMC Theatres, said in a press release. "We're excited to give fans the opportunity to watch esports' biggest stage unfold live on massive screens, surrounded by fellow Rocket League fans.”
A full list of the participating theaters can be found at the link embedded here.
